# @tscad/plugins

[![Homepage](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-default)](https://tscad.vercel.app)

Example plugins for tscad: WebAssembly components written in Rust

<!-- #endregion header -->

Plugins are WebAssembly components implementing one world of [`wit/tscad-plugin.wit`](../wit/tscad-plugin.wit).
Each one is also a package (`@tscad/plugin-<name>`), which tscad finds among a model's dependencies
by the `"tscad": { "plugin": "./dist" }` field in its package.json.
They run sandboxed: a plugin can only call the kernel's shape API, with no file or network access.

| Plugin                         | World       | What it does                                                                              |
| ------------------------------ | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`grid`](grid)                 | `operation` | Repeats its children on a grid: `grid({ nx, ny, dx, dy }, ...)` from `@tscad/plugin-grid` |
| [`export-3mf`](export-3mf)     | `exporter`  | 3MF export with merged vertices and colors                                                |
| [`printability`](printability) | `analysis`  | Overhangs, bed contact and fit for 3D printing                                            |

`bun run build` compiles each crate for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, wraps it as a component (`jco new`)
and transpiles it to JS + core wasm in `<plugin>/dist` (`jco transpile`), which
[`@tscad/plugin-host`](../packages/plugin-host) loads in Bun and browsers. For a plugin with options,
it also generates `<plugin>/dist/<plugin>.wit` and a typed `<plugin>/dist/index.ts` from the options
schema the plugin reports ([`options-wit.ts`](options-wit.ts)).

To write a plugin, see [Writing a plugin](https://tscad.vercel.app/docs/guides/plugins#writing-a-plugin).
